title: Samsung Smart Switch Now Transfers Passwords, eSIM Data From iPhone to Galaxy
excerpt: One UI 9 update eliminates the need to install an app on iPhones, adding QR-code-based wireless transfer for passwords, passkeys, and eSIM profiles.
body:
• Samsung's Smart Switch on One UI 9 now transfers passwords, passkeys, call history, and eSIM profiles from iPhone to Galaxy devices.
  • iPhone users no longer need to install a separate app — scanning a QR code on the new Galaxy starts the wireless transfer.
  • The update launches on the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, and Z Flip8, with Quick Share gaining AirDrop compatibility.

Samsung has overhauled its Smart Switch data-transfer tool with One UI 9, adding the ability to move passwords, passkeys, call history, accessibility settings, and eSIM information from an iPhone to a new Galaxy device. The update ships with the eighth-generation Galaxy Z series — the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold8, and Galaxy Z Flip8.

No App Install Required

The most visible change is procedural. Previous versions of Smart Switch required iPhone users to download the Smart Switch app from the App Store before initiating a transfer. One UI 9 eliminates that step entirely. Users scan a QR code displayed on their new Galaxy device, tap “Transfer to Android” on their iPhone, and the wireless connection begins — no cables, no adapters, no third-party downloads.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=93HqxJldTHg

“For users switching from iOS to Galaxy, being able to bring existing data and settings across easily is an important part of the experience,” Samsung said in a statement announcing the feature.

Passwords, Passkeys, and eSIM

Smart Switch has long handled the basics — photos, messages, contacts, calendars, and apps. The One UI 9 update adds several categories that previously required manual recreation on a new device.

Saved passwords and passkeys transfer over, reducing the tedium of logging back into accounts one by one. Call history carries across, preserving a record that many users rely on. Accessibility settings — font sizes, display adjustments, hearing accommodations — move with the user, eliminating the need to reconfigure a personalized experience from scratch.

The eSIM transfer is arguably the most consequential addition. For supported carriers, users can migrate their existing mobile number and service plan to the Galaxy without visiting a store or waiting for a physical SIM. Samsung maintains a list of eligible carriers at samsung.com/esim-support, and availability varies by region.

Familiar Feel From Day One

Beyond raw data transfer, One UI 9 lets switchers carry over interface preferences including swipe gestures and home screen layout. Samsung's Good Lock customization app provides further control over the home screen, app switching behavior, and navigation — options designed to reduce the adjustment period for users accustomed to iOS conventions.

Quick Share, Samsung's file-sharing feature, has also been updated. Devices running One UI 9 and One UI 8.5 gain cross-platform sharing with Apple's AirDrop, allowing Galaxy and iPhone users to exchange files directly.

Competitive Context

The update arrives as the smartphone market's switching dynamics intensify. Apple has tightened its ecosystem grip with features like iMessage and AirDrop, making platform exits more difficult. Samsung's response targets the friction points that have historically discouraged iPhone users from trying Galaxy devices — the lost passwords, the carrier store trip for a new SIM, the hours spent reconfiguring accessibility options.

The Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, priced as Samsung's premium foldable, benefits most from reducing switching barriers. Samsung is betting that users willing to spend on high-end hardware are also the most likely to demand a seamless transition.

The Smart Switch update is available now on Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, and Z Flip8 devices running One UI 9.
nri_angle: The update is relevant for Indian-American users considering switching from iPhone to Samsung Galaxy devices, particularly with eSIM transfer simplifying carrier setup.
